correctness.rationale: Uniform vertex signs on C5 yield 16 equally likely even-parity edge-sign patterns. The scalar quadratic response S has five affine t levels with multiplicities 1,4,6,4,1. The finite swapping/rearrangement inequality minimizes E[SS′] by countermonotone sorting; each scalar atom has equally many uniform sign-vector lifts, so the scalar optimum lifts to two fully uniform Rademacher marginals without imposing probe independence. An independent 32-vector exact rational computation confirms V*(t)=4t² for 0<t<=1; 3+(t-2)² for 1<=t<=3; 4 for t>=3, including ties, and fixed flip optimum 4min(1,t²). For 1<t<3 their difference is (t-1)(3-t), peaking at 25% of 4 at t=2. On even cycles a checkerboard sign flip cancels every edge; for C3 a four-valued parity distribution gives 4 min(weight²). The claim is minimal among simple cycles (C3,C4), not among all matrices or graphs.
